Concavity gives the iff one-step invariant interval condition via h'(R); radius inequalities prove full convergence within it. Numerical checks support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The verified literature already contains general period-two existence, elasticity-based local stability and almost-everywhere global attraction. These are acknowledged and not counted as new. The final contribution is the sharp if-and-only-if one-step invariant-radius interval for the specific fractional kinetic family, its exponent 1/4 dividing uniform and finite-parameter trapping, the exact finite-step globally captured superattracting tuning, and the nonzero fourth-order two-step error coefficient. Neither relevant inspected full text states or logically fixes that sharper radius-invariance property. Exact searches and semantic research-record queries revealed no covering occurrence; absence of hits is not a general priority proof.
residual_risks: The conditional 1/4 boundary is an exact special-family calculation; unindexed independent analyses of fractional kinetic maps could contain it.

value.rationale: The sharp global no-overshoot frontier distinguishes dynamics on two sides of an already known locally stable cycle and addresses whether all subcycle amplitudes remain trapped. The a=1/4 exponent division is a natural regularization-design boundary. At a finite critical tuning, all generic real initial conditions enter a globally controlled region and converge with exact fourth-order physical return, a substantial rate improvement with an explicit coefficient. This is a structural and rate result, not a bare existence or local-stability corollary.
